name: Venezuela
sources: GDP $48.6bn and 19.8m people (World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.CD and SP.POP.TOTL, 1990; exact prints $48.607bn and 19,827,010). GDP grew 6.5% in 1990 on the oil price spike that followed Iraq's invasion of Kuwait, after contracting 8.6% in 1989; the underlying TFP trend is negative, at -0.4%/yr, because per-capita output in 1990 was below its 1977 level.

Inflation 40.7% is the Banco Central de Venezuela CPI annual average for 1990, following 81% in 1989 when the Perez government freed prices. interest_rate 40% is the commercial deposit benchmark after rate ceilings were lifted in 1989.

Tax take 22% of GDP: almost all of it is PDVSA's remittance, and non-oil tax revenue was under 8% of GDP — there was no income tax administration worth the name. That dependence is the whole political economy of the file.
Debt 0.60: external debt about $33bn at end-1990 (World Bank), roughly 68% of GDP, of which the public share is around $26bn. The Brady restructuring was signed in December 1990.

Oil 2.14 mbd of crude in 1990 (OPEC Annual Statistical Bulletin), rising through the year as Venezuela took up Iraqi and Kuwaiti quota. Public investment 8% of GDP is mostly PDVSA and the Guayana state industries.

Stability 40: the Caracazo of 27 February 1989, in which the army fired on rioters in Caracas and killed several hundred, had broken the legitimacy of the Punto Fijo two-party settlement. Two coup attempts follow in February and November 1992, led by officers who were serving in 1990. They are not scripted — the model has to produce them.
Defence 2.1% of GDP and strength 8. Separatism 0.02.

pop_growth_1990 = 2.6116%/yr. Compound annual growth of World Bank SP.POP.TOTL, series VEN (Venezuela, RB): 17,008,841 in 1984 to 19,348,921 in 1989 — the five years ending on the eve of the 1 January 1990 start date. See EconomyRecord::pop_growth_1990 in spheres-sim/src/data/mod.rs for why the window ends in 1989 and not with the single-year 1990 rate.

reserves_bn = 8.702 ($bn). Total reserves including gold, VEN, 1989: US$8701843814.76 (World Bank World Development Indicators series FI.RES.TOTL.CD, 'Total reserves (includes gold, current US$)', retrieved from the World Bank API on 2026-09-02; indicator lastupdated 2026-07-13). THE 1989 OBSERVATION AND NOT THE 1990 ONE: a reserve is a stock, and the stock on the morning of the 1 January 1990 start date is the end-1989 figure - the same reasoning pop_growth_1990 above gives for ending its window on 31 December 1989. LIMIT STATED: this series is official reserve assets. Sovereign wealth fund balances are not in it and none has been added, because no audited 1990 balance could be sourced for any of them; where that materially understates a state's usable stock it is reported rather than estimated (iron rule 4).

note: 1990 TECHNOLOGY: AUTHORED, NOT DERIVED. What this nation knew on 1 January 1990 is transcribed and sourced grant by grant, exactly like every other 1990 figure in this file, and is not read off tfp_trend - there was never a code path from the trend to the known set, and the zero that stood there was a claim about the world rather than an absence of one (BIBLE section 8 and iron rule 4, both amended 2026-08-30). THE PREDICATE IS SPLIT, and split by the technology's OWN EFFECT TYPE so that it is mechanically computable and never a per-nation judgement call. A node whose effects include MilitaryEfficiency, MilitaryStrength, DiffusionEmission or CostReduction is SOVEREIGNTY-SIDE: holding it means this nation could PRODUCE it, so operating an imported article does not qualify. Every other node is USE-SIDE: deployed and in operational use here is enough, whoever built it, because the effect such a node pays is a productivity, health or output effect and that effect is real in the country where the machine runs. Of the 48 technologies the tree lets anyone hold in 1990, 17 are sovereignty-side and 31 are use-side.

DATA-KEYED TAIL NATION. This nation is outside the 29 authored majors, so nothing here was authored technology by technology: a grant is made only where one of two named published global series supports it, and nothing is modelled, estimated or interpolated. A short list, or an empty one, is the correct outcome of that rule and not a gap in the work.

Data-keyed tail nation: not one of the 29 authored majors. Only the two series named in ruling 3 were consulted - WHO/UNICEF WUENIC DTP3 1990 and World Bank IT.CEL.SETS. Nothing was modelled, estimated or interpolated, and no other evidence was admitted. ISO3 key used for both series: VEN.
WUENIC DTP3 1990 = 63% against the 80% UCI-1990 threshold: refused.
IT.CEL.SETS at 31 December 1989 = 3685 against a threshold of any positive count: comm_cellular_analogue GRANTED.

The other 46 grantable 1990 technologies are BLANK for this nation by design, not by oversight: the 17 sovereignty-side entries are unreachable by any use-in-operation series, and no published global series was named that keys the remaining 29 use-side entries.

granted.source: World Bank WDI IT.CEL.SETS 'Mobile cellular subscriptions', retrieved from the World Bank indicator API (api.worldbank.org/v2), source id 2, lastupdated 2026-07-13. Series values: VEN, 1989 = 3685 subscriptions and 1990 = 7422 subscriptions. The series is a YEAR-END STOCK, so the 1989 figure describes 31 December 1989, i.e. the game's start instant of 1 January 1990: a network was carrying paying subscribers before the start date. All cellular in service at that date was analogue (NMT, AMPS, TACS, C-Netz, RTMS); GSM had no commercial service anywhere until mid-1991.
